subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add route/ACP binding `tools.allow` and `tools.deny` as a supported security boundary, or should this need use existing group, sender, session, or conversation-identity policy instead?
rationale: The request adds a new public config and authorization surface whose precedence overlaps existing tool-policy layers, so automation should not choose the permanent security guarantee or owner boundary.

options.title: Design Binding Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Policy Surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group/channel, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported tool restriction path.

options.title: Defer To Conversation Identity
options.body: Block this slice on the broader scoped conversation identity/capability design if maintainers want one authorization model instead of a binding-specific layer.

recommendation.title: Design Binding Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history around scoped conversation capability and the related product/security decision surface.
